text:
Mira: Follow-up from today's RFC retrospective. Two concrete asks: design a compact fingerprint migration path for older clients, and clarify how SDKs should expose per-request precision hints without blowing up the hot path. Capturing ideas here.

Sam: Hot path constraints first: runtime must only read a fixed-size fingerprint struct (u64 id, u32 mask, u32 fallback) that is memory-aligned and constant-time to access. No heap, no JSON parsing. Any richer metadata stays in a separate slow path.

Anya: For migration: some customers on Dedicated/Private might run older agents that don't understand the new fingerprint. Proposal: fingerprint v1 (legacy) -> allow a compatibility map published by control plane. Map entry: legacy_hash -> latest_fingerprint. Runtime should look up legacy_hash in an inline small hashmap when bootstrapping, not per-request.

Kyle: How to publish compatibility maps safely? We should publish them as part of the bundle and expose a small monotonic "compat_version" in headers so we can roll forward and revoke mappings if bad. Also include TTL for each mapping so clients periodically refresh.

Mira: Good. Also want a strategy for opaque SDK surface: developers want to request "prefer_low_bit" or pin a profile id. We shouldn't force SDKs to send big profiles or negotiate on each request. Suggest header-based opt-in: x-precision-preference: prefer_low_bit|prefer_high_quality|profile:<id>. Simple string. SDKs can expose a typed enum but send the small header.

Sam: Agree. Add that the runtime must ignore unknown profile ids when running in offline mode and fall back to pinned default. That makes private installs safe.

Anya: Observability: include three headers in responses when relevant: x-precision-applied (fp8|int8|4bit), x-precision-reason (small code), x-precision-fingerprint (hex). Keep values compact.

Kyle: For legacy clients, responses could include a compatibility hint header x-precision-compat: map_version=42 so monitoring can correlate.

Mira: Edge case: long-lived streaming calls (chat). We need re-resolution without blocking. Proposal: runtime spawns a background resolver thread that watches latest fingerprint + compat map and updates an atomic pointer used by requests. Re-resolve triggers when token count crosses threshold or on explicit SDK heartbeat.

Sam: Implementation note: make the atomic pointer point to an mmap'ed structure for Dedicated so update is pointer swap and no allocs. Provide a tiny C header so third-party runtimes can use it.

Anya: Security: signed bundles must include a digest of the compat map; otherwise MITM could map legacy ids to unsafe low-bit paths. Use ed25519 signatures and include signer key id in the bundle manifest.

Kyle: UX: Console should show a migration table per client version showing which clients are still on legacy fingerprints and which have migrated. That helps target upgrade campaigns.

deploy-bot: Rolling canary: compat-map-v2 -> 2% at 2026-04-03T00:30Z :satellite:

Mira: Action items: Sam to draft C header + atomic layout; Anya to draft compat-map TTL and revocation semantics; Kyle to add console mockups for migration table; I'll incorporate header names into the API doc and open PR.

Sam: I'll also run a microbenchmark for pointer-swap vs lock and publish numbers.

Anya: I'll add a regression test to ensure mapping revocation triggers fallback and alerting.

Mira: Thanks all — will sync tomorrow at 9am PT for final sign-off.
